From: Sara Park <sara.park@helixbio.com>

Cc: procurement@helixbio.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit onboarding and evidence delivery schedule

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a handful of follow-ups before legal will sign the order form: primarily around the security exhibit and audit / inspection mechanics. I attached a short spreadsheet with our initial questions. High-level items:

- SOC 2: do you provide a current Type II report and how soon can we receive it after contract execution?
- Pen test: we prefer a 30-day notice window and a scoped staging environment; what are your typical windows and guardrails?
- Evidence cadence: procurement expects a clear delivery rhythm (what artifacts come monthly vs ad-hoc).
- Audit rights: our GC wants the inspection language limited to production-scope and sample-based inspection rather than full tenant inspection.

Would appreciate a short proposal from your side that we can take to our GC — ideally something that maps to an MSA + Order Form change and an evidence delivery checklist.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Park
Head of Security Programs, Helix Bio
attachments: Helix_Questions.xlsx

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@helixbio.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit onboarding and evidence delivery schedule

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the clear list — I skimmed the spreadsheet and put together a concise, multi-phase approach below that should map cleanly into the MSA (exhibit) + Order Form. I attached our current security exhibit draft (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1.pdf) for context.

Proposed multi-phase onboarding (high level):
1) Phase A (pre-execution / immediate):
   - Provide latest SOC 2 Type II attestation and control summary within 10 business days of counter-signature.
   - Deliver a one-page controls mapping that highlights customer-facing protections (encryption, network segmentation, RBAC).
2) Phase B (staged pen test):
   - Schedule a limited penetration test window (recommended 30–45 day lead time) in a staging environment; Redwood provides scoped access and sampling rules.
   - Results shared as a redacted executive summary plus remediation timeline. Full findings can be reviewed under NDA / secure share if needed.
3) Phase C (operational evidence cadence):
   - First 8 weeks: weekly artifact bundle (SOC logs summary, change-control snapshot, incident posture summary) while onboarding is active.
   - Ongoing: monthly evidence packet (attestation updates, patching summary, pen-test status) and ad-hoc items as agreed in the exhibit.

Contract asks we usually see and our proposals:
- Limit inspection to "sampled evidence" and tenant-level sampling rather than broad unbounded inspection.
- Pen test notice: 30 days preferred; Redwood will offer a list of acceptable windows and a staging host list.
- Evidence delivery: define a "standard evidence packet" in the exhibit with an owner and SLA for delivery (we propose 10 business days).

Ben — can you propose specific redline language for the exhibit/Order Form to cover the above? Marissa, flagging for customer success onboarding timeline coordination.

Sara — if the above aligns, we can produce (a) redline-ready exhibit language, (b) a 1-page runbook describing evidence handoff, and (c) a proposed pen-test calendar for June.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@helixbio.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit onboarding and ordered evidence delivery

Sara / Lauren —

Thanks for the outline. From a contracting perspective I recommend the following redlines to the security exhibit and the Order Form so Helix's GC has concrete language to review:

1) Definitions (Order Form / Exhibit)
   - "Inspection Window": defined as a mutually agreed 48–72 hour window for technical access during which Redwood will assign an on-call engineer.
   - "Sampled Evidence": defined as artifacts scoped to a statistically representative sample of customer instances; full tenant-wide forensic access requires a separate legal request with 30 days' notice.

2) Penetration Testing
   - Redwood agrees to coordinate a staging pen test with at least 30 days' notice. Redwood will provide target IPs and a list of services in scope.
   - Any penetration testing that requires access to customer data or forensics will be limited to redacted findings in contract deliverables; detailed findings available under NDA.

3) SOC 2 and Deliverables
   - Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and control mappings within 10 business days of request after contract signature.
   - Standard evidence packet defined in Exhibit A, delivered with a 10-business-day SLA unless otherwise agreed.

4) Access Controls and Limitations
   - Explicitly state that Redwood's network and production environment remain segregated and that customer data access for inspection is scoped and time-boxed.

5) Escalation & Scheduling
   - Add a procurement/ops contact block and a clause that Redwood may propose alternate windows if the initially requested dates conflict with critical maintenance.

I attached a document with tracked redlines you can share with Helix's GC — it contains snippet text you can paste into the exhibit. If Helix wants broader inspection rights we can discuss additional controls and cost implications (e.g., additional on-call coverage, expanded evidence extraction).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: security-exhibit-redline.docx
